where.description:
Where counts only the calls whose arguments meet this CEL condition,
read as inputs, as in the plugin's manifest: what was sent, not only
that something was ("inputs.children == '5,8'").

EffectCount.description: EffectCount is how many successful calls an action must have.

metadata.description: Metadata names the suite; its namespace is the agent under test.

EvalSuite.description:
EvalSuite tests an agent with whole conversations (RFC-0002, level 4). A
scenario plays a user against the agent's Functions, with plugins
replaced by sandboxes that keep state, and checks what happened: the
effects, the messages, the invariants every agent must keep, and the cost.

description.description: Description says what the suite covers.

now.description:
Now is the clock of every scenario (RFC 3339 with offset), so dates
in the conversation mean the same thing on every run. A scenario can
set its own.

sandboxes.description:
Sandboxes replace plugins with stateful fakes written in Starlark.
Each scenario starts from the sandbox's initial state.

team.description:
Team plays the business's team in llm scenarios, for a task the
scenario's humans have no answer for (team-001). A model answers
only from Facts, and says so when they do not settle the task. A
task asking for a value gets one, in the task's format.

status.description: Status is the final status of the last run.

effects.description: Effects counts successful calls per action.

milestones.description: Milestones counts recorded milestones per subject kind and name.

never.description: Never lists actions that must not be called at all.

says.description: Says lists texts that must appear in some message to the user.

notSays.description: NotSays lists texts no message to the user may contain.

skipInvariants.description:
Invariants to skip; every invariant runs unless listed here, with a
reason in the scenario's description.

budget.description: Budget fails the scenario when exceeded.

count.description: Count of milestones recorded in the scenario.

MilestoneCount.description: MilestoneCount expects a number of milestones.

name.description:
Name of the resource, unique per kind within its namespace. Lowercase
letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

namespace.description: Namespace the resource belongs to, usually one per customer.

labels.description: Labels are free-form key/value pairs for selecting and grouping.

goal.description: Goal is what the user wants from the conversation.

style.description: Style is how they write (short WhatsApp messages, typos, formal).

knows.description: Knows holds the facts the user can tell: dates, names, preferences.

language.description: Language of the user's messages (default: Brazilian Portuguese).

Persona.description:
Persona is a simulated user: what they want, how they write and what
they know. The simulator shares what it knows only when it is natural
or asked, and never invents facts outside it.

plugin.description: Plugin is the PluginManifest name this sandbox replaces.

script.description: Script is the .star file, relative to this file.

state.description: State is the initial state, a map the functions read and change.

Sandbox.description:
Sandbox fakes a plugin. The script has one function per action, named
after it with "-" as "_" (list-upcoming-appointments becomes
list_upcoming_appointments), taking state and the action's arguments as
keyword arguments. It may change state and returns the output; it calls
definite(code, message) or ambiguous(message) to fail like a real system.

id.description: ID names the scenario in reports.

caller.description: Caller is the verified identity of the user.

state.description:
State changes the sandboxes' state for this scenario, per plugin:
its top-level keys replace the suite's (an outage, an empty agenda).

simulator.description:
Simulator plays the user. scripted replays fixed turns; llm has a
model play the persona until its goal is met (RFC-0002), after the
turns, when there are any.

turns.description: Turns are played in order. A scripted scenario needs at least one.

persona.description: Persona is the user the llm simulator plays.

maxTurns.description: MaxTurns bounds the llm simulator's messages (default 12).

humans.description:
Humans answer, in order, the tasks the agent hands to a person
during an llm scenario: a value such as true, "o2" or {"ok": true}.
A question for the team (an answer task) takes the next text, a task
asking for a value (input) the next non-text. When none fits, the
scenario ends at that task.

expect.description: Expect is checked after the last turn.

ScenarioBudget.description: ScenarioBudget bounds what a scenario may consume.

facts.description:
Facts is a Markdown file, relative to the suite, holding everything
the team knows about the business and its world.

SimTeam.description: SimTeam is the simulated team of an EvalSuite.

payload.description: Payload is event.payload for a webhook trigger.

TriggerTurn.description: TriggerTurn fires a Trigger in a scenario.

user.description: User is what the user writes.

advance.description:
Advance moves the scenario's clock forward (Go duration, e.g. 48h)
and runs the scheduler: waits that come due wake, schedules start,
stuck subjects escalate. The turn's expectations read what they sent.

trigger.description:
Trigger fires a Trigger as if it came due (a schedule) or was called
(a webhook, with this payload, unsigned in tests). A run it starts in
another conversation becomes the scenario's conversation, so later
user turns reply to it.

human.description:
Human answers the human task the run waits for: a value such as true,
"o2" or {"happened": true}.

expect.description: Expect is checked right after this turn.

Turn.description:
Turn is one event. Exactly one of user, human, advance and trigger must
be set.

status.description: Status is the run's status after the turn.

routed.description: Routed is the Function this turn started through the router.

handoff.description:
Handoff is the free mode's decision this turn: "answer", or the
Function of freeMode.functions it started (such as asking a person).

says.description:
Says lists texts that must each appear (ignoring case) in a message
sent to the user this turn.

notSays.description: NotSays lists texts no message to the user may contain this turn.

queue.description: Queue is a human queue that must receive a task this turn.
